Brings Axis **network cameras**, **door stations** (network intercoms) and
**network speakers** into Gladys, **locally**, through their VAPIX API: camera
images, motion, objects, persons and vehicles seen by AXIS Object Analytics,
the PIR sensor, sound detection, tampering, day and night, the digital inputs,
the ring of a door station, the infrared light, the audio clips of the
speakers, and the outputs (relays) for your scenes. No cloud account, nothing
leaves your network.

> **Developed without the hardware: feedback welcome.** This integration was
> written from the public VAPIX documentation, the Home Assistant `axis`
> integration and the `axis` library by Kane610 (with their real device
> answers), without an Axis device at hand. If something does not work as
> described, please open an issue on
> [github.com/guim31/gladys-axis/issues](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-axis/issues)
> with the integration logs (`LOG_LEVEL=debug`).
>
> This integration is not affiliated with Axis Communications. AXIS is a
> trademark of Axis AB.

## What you need

- An Axis camera, door station or speaker reachable from Gladys on your
  network, its web page working (port 80, or 443 in HTTPS).
- A **local account** of the device. An **operator** account is enough for
  everything (images, events, infrared light, outputs, clips); a viewer
  account can only read. The first account of an Axis device is `root`:
  creating a dedicated `gladys` operator account is better.
- For the live events: AXIS OS 11 or later uses the WebSocket event stream
  over the web port; older firmwares use the RTSP metadata stream, so the
  RTSP port (554 by default) must be reachable too.
- Gladys **5.1 or later**.

## Set up

### Settings

In Gladys, open the integration, then its **Configuration** tab:

- **Device addresses**: the IP addresses (or names) of your devices,
  separated by commas, e.g. `192.168.1.90, 192.168.1.91`. Add `:port` if the
  web page is not on port 80, and `https://` for HTTPS (the self-signed
  certificate of the device is accepted). Never put the password in the
  address.
- **User name** and **Password**: the local account of the devices. The
  password is sent to the devices only, never to a cloud.
- **Other device addresses**, **Their user name**, **Their password**:
  optional, for devices (a door station, for instance) with other credentials.
- **Camera images**: how often the image of each camera added to Gladys is
  refreshed (every 5 minutes by default, or only on events). A person
  detected or a ring always sends a fresh image.
- **Allow driving the outputs**: off by default. On a door station the
  outputs (relays) open the door or the gate: they are only driven by the
  scene action, once this setting is on, and are never a switch.
- **Language of the names**: the language of the feature names (set when a
  device is added) and of the texts sent to scenes. French by default.

Then open the **Discovery** tab: each camera (each video source of a
multi-sensor camera), door station and speaker is listed. Add the ones you
want.

### Configuration actions

- **Test the connection**: reads every device again and reports, one line
  per device, its model, its video sources and how its live events arrive
  (WebSocket or RTSP). After a refused password, it is the way to try again
  once the password is fixed.
- **Search the network**: asks Gladys to look for the Axis devices of the
  network (mDNS `_axis-video._tcp` and UPnP), and lists them: configured, to
  add (copy its address into **Device addresses**), or found at a new
  address. Bonjour and UPnP must be on on the devices (they are by default).
- **Audio clips**: lists the audio clips stored on each device, by number
  and name, for the **Play an audio clip** scene action.
- **Show the video stream address**: the RTSP address of a camera, to use
  with the "RTSP camera" integration of Gladys. The password is replaced by
  `PASSWORD`: type it yourself.

## The devices

### Cameras

Each video source becomes a device. Its features, each one only when the
camera has it:

| Feature              | What it shows                                                                 |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Image**            | The camera image, refreshed as set in **Camera images**                       |
| **Online**           | The camera answers                                                            |
| **Motion**           | AXIS Video Motion Detection, the guard profiles, the ONVIF motion rules       |
| **Object analytics** | An AXIS Object Analytics scenario is triggered                                |
| **Person**           | An object classified as a person (AXIS Object Analytics)                      |
| **Vehicle**          | An object classified as a vehicle (AXIS Object Analytics)                     |
| **PIR sensor**       | The PIR sensor of the camera                                                  |
| **Sound detection**  | The sound level trigger of the camera                                         |
| **Tampering**        | The camera was moved, covered or blinded                                      |
| **Night mode**       | The camera is in night mode (infrared cut filter removed)                     |
| **Infrared light**   | The infrared illuminator: on or off from Gladys                               |
| **Input**            | Each digital input, named as on the camera (e.g. `Garden gate`), or "Input 1" |

The detections a camera reports in its events add their feature (one sensor
per event present): if a feature you expect is missing, trigger the
detection once, then open **Discovery** again and update the device.

The outputs (relays) of a camera are never a feature: see the **Drive an
output (relay)** scene action.

### Door stations

An Axis door station (A8105-E, A8207-VE, I8016-LVE, I8116-E…) is a camera
with a **Doorbell ring** feature: it goes to 1 when someone presses the call
button, then back to 0 after ten seconds, and fires the **Someone rang the
door station** trigger with a fresh image. The call button is recognised
when its input is named so (`Call button`, `Doorbell`, `Appel`…), or as the
first input of an AXIS I8116-E. Its door relay is an output: see **Drive an
output (relay)**.

### Network speakers

An Axis network speaker (C1310-E, C1410…) becomes a device with the
**Online** feature; it plays its audio clips through the **Play an audio
clip** scene action.

## Dashboard

The **Axis** widget shows the devices online, the persons and rings of the
last 24 hours, the latest ones with their image, and the state of each
device. In its settings, choose one device, or leave it empty for all.

The camera images and every feature can also be added to the dashboard with
the usual Gladys boxes.

## Scenes

### Triggers

- **Person detected by a camera**: a camera saw a person (AXIS Object
  Analytics or a guard profile). Filter on the camera; the variables give the
  camera name and the name of the scenario. The camera image is fresh when
  the scene starts, so "send the camera image" sends the right one. One event
  per camera every 15 seconds at most.
- **Someone rang the door station**: the call button was pressed. Filter on
  the door station; the variable gives its name. The image is fresh too.

The features (**Motion**, **Person**, **Input**…) can also start a scene with
the usual "a device state changes" trigger.

### Actions

- **Refresh a camera image**: takes a fresh image of a camera for Gladys, to
  send it in a message right after.
- **Play an audio clip**: plays a clip stored on an Axis speaker, door
  station or camera, by its number or its name (empty: the first clip). The
  **Audio clips** configuration action lists them.
- **Drive an output (relay)**: a pulse of 1, 3 or 10 seconds, or activate or
  deactivate an output, numbered from 1 among the outputs of the device. On a
  door station, this opens the door: it only works once **Allow driving the
  outputs** is on, and the command is sent once, never repeated.

### Scene ideas

- **Ring at the door**: when someone rang the door station, send the door
  station image in a message, and play a chime on the speaker of the living
  room with **Play an audio clip**.
- **Night watch**: when a person is detected by the driveway camera between
  midnight and 6 am, turn on the garden lights, play the "Warning" clip on the
  horn speaker and send the camera image.
- **Opening the gate for a known arrival**: when your phone arrives home,
  drive output 1 of the door station with a pulse of 1 second (only after
  allowing it, and only if you accept the risk of a scene that opens a door).

## Live video

Gladys shows camera images, not a live video stream. For live video, use the
**Show the video stream address** action and add the RTSP address to the
"RTSP camera" integration of Gladys.

## Refresh and limits

- The live events arrive as they happen: WebSocket on AXIS OS 11 and later,
  RTSP metadata stream otherwise, always one connection per device opened by
  Gladys (nothing to open in your router). A stream lost is reopened (after
  5 seconds, then up to 5 minutes between tries).
- The integration reads the inputs and the infrared light every 5 minutes,
  every minute while an event stream is down. It never waits for Gladys to
  poll the devices.
- The images are taken at 640 pixels wide at most, scaled by the camera
  (Gladys takes images of 150 KB at most), never more often than every 6
  seconds per camera.
- A value that does not change is sent again every 6 hours, so Gladys never
  shows it as old.
- VAPIX has no quota. Axis devices block an address for a while after
  repeated wrong passwords: the integration stops at the first refusal and
  only tries again on a new configuration or with **Test the connection**.

## Troubleshooting

- **"User name or password refused"**: check them on the web page of the
  device, fix them in the configuration, then use **Test the connection**.
- **"This account is not allowed to do this"**: use an operator account.
- **The device does not answer**: check its address, its port, and that
  Gladys reaches it (same network, no firewall in between).
- **"Live events are interrupted"**: on an older firmware, check that the
  RTSP port (554) is reachable and that RTSP is enabled on the device. Inputs
  and the infrared light are still read every minute.
- **A detection is missing**: enable it on the camera (AXIS Object
  Analytics scenario, VMD profile, sound level trigger), trigger it once,
  then update the device in **Discovery**.
- **The ring of a door station is not seen**: name the input of the call
  button `Call button` on the door station, then use **Test the connection**.
- **Details**: set `LOG_LEVEL=debug` on the integration to see every event
  and every read in its logs. Passwords never appear there.

## Limits

- Developed without the hardware: the topics, the event streams and the
  call button rule come from the documentation and from the work of Home
  Assistant, not from a test on a real device.
- No live video in Gladys (camera images only), no pan, tilt or zoom.
- The outputs are a scene action only, by design: never a switch, never
  available to a voice assistant.
- The audio clips are played, not uploaded: record them on the device.
- On a multi-sensor camera, the AXIS Object Analytics features first show on
  the first video source; the others gain them at their first detection.
- The devices from the network search are not added by themselves: copy
  their address into the configuration.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Axis asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your Axis devices | `section` | No | Axis cameras, door stations (intercoms) and network speakers, on your network, through their VAPIX API. Use a local account of the device, ideally a dedicated operator account. Nothing goes through a cloud. The "Search the network" action lists the Axis devices it finds. |
| Device addresses | `string` | Yes | IP addresses or names, separated by commas, with :port if not 80, https:\/\/ for HTTPS. |
| User name | `string` | No |  |
| Password | `secret` | Yes | Sent to the devices only, never to a cloud. Axis devices block an address after repeated wrong passwords: the integration stops at the first refusal. |
| Devices with other credentials | `section` | No | Optional: a door station or a camera whose user name or password differs from the ones above. |
| Other device addresses | `string` | No |  |
| Their user name | `string` | No |  |
| Their password | `secret` | No |  |
| Camera images | `select` | No | How often the image of each camera added to Gladys is refreshed. A person or a ring always sends a fresh one. |
| Allow driving the outputs | `boolean` | No | Lets scenes drive the outputs (relays): on a door station they open the door or the gate. Scene action only, never a switch. Off by default. |
| Language of the names | `select` | No | Language of the feature names and of the texts sent to scenes. Names are set when a device is added. |

## How to install Axis in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Axis appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-axis:1.0.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-axis](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-axis).

Axis requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Axis is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [guim31](https://github.com/guim31), not by the Gladys core team.
